leading_hypothesis.claim: If fork/clone is allowed while an execution capability is live, effect authority requires an explicit process-incarnation or equivalent non-inheritable capability boundary; child state defaults fail-closed until explicit re-admission/delegation.

strongest_counterhypothesis.claim: A simpler production invariant can forbid and measurably enforce all fork/clone paths while FrankExecutionLease/effect capability is live, making extra process-incarnation machinery unnecessary.
strongest_counterhypothesis.discriminator: Exact target PR233-style child test plus current spawn/fork surface census.

architecture_delta_candidate.name: FORK_SAFE_EXECUTION_CAPABILITY_BOUNDARY
rules: Fork/process cloning never implicitly delegates effect authority.
If child execution is unsupported, inherited Frank effect/execution capability is invalidated before semantic/effect execution.
Child invalidation must not explicitly LOCK_UN a flock open-file-description shared with the live parent; cleanup must not semantically release the parent's V15/V16 execution.
If child delegation is supported, require explicit process-incarnation/delegation receipt and process-shared commit/release semantics; threading.RLock is not cross-process serialization.
Outcome observation/reconciliation remains admissible after authority turnover because evidence is not authority.
At-fork hooks are only a candidate mechanism; native/third-party fork and exec/spawn paths require measurement.
Prefer a measured no-fork invariant if it dominates the more complex process-incarnation design.
